expectations.text: Flags that transfer()'s fromAccount and toAccount are both plain strings and can be swapped silently
expectations.evidence: "Call `transfer(to, from, amt)` — two adjacent `string`s, compiles fine. Device: Branded `AccountId`, a single object parameter" with code example

expectations.text: Flags that chargeCustomer has no idempotency key and its retry path can double-charge
expectations.evidence: "Stripe succeeded, the response was lost, the retry charges again. No idempotency key. Device: Require an idempotency key, never catch-and-null"

expectations.text: Flags the catch block that returns null as swallowing the error
expectations.evidence: "failure returns `null`" in title and "And on failure the function returns `null`, so the caller gets a falsy 'charge' and no error — `handleWebhook` ignores the return entirely"

expectations.text: Flags money being held as a JS number (float) rather than integer minor units
expectations.evidence: "Also `amountCents: number` accepts `19.99` (dollars) with no complaint. Device: Options object, `Cents` branded integer type validated at the boundary"

expectations.text: Flags the interpolated raw SQL in purgeCanceledAccounts
expectations.evidence: "Also string-interpolated SQL (`$executeRawUnsafe`). Device: use the parameterised client; delete by the IDs you just fetched, not a second predicate" with code example

expectations.text: Flags the non-exhaustive switch over subscription status
expectations.evidence: "The DB row gets the string anyway; the switch matches nothing; features stay whatever they were. Device: `status: "active" | "canceled" | ...` union, exhaustive switch with `never` default"

expectations.text: Flags JSON.parse of the webhook body as unvalidated external input
expectations.evidence: "No signature check, `JSON.parse` of untrusted input, `event.data.amount` typed `any`. Device: `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent(body, sig, secret)` before anything else"

expectations.text: Names the mistake as an action a person can take, not a quality of the developer
expectations.evidence: "Call `purgeCanceledAccounts()`", "Call `transfer(to, from, amt)`", "Pass `retry = true`", "Accept a POST body from anyone" — all named as actions

expectations.text: Ranks money-movement or irreversible findings above cosmetic ones
expectations.evidence: "the top three (unbounded raw-SQL purge, non-atomic swappable transfer, idempotency-free retry) are the money-losers"; items 1-4 money-related, items 5-7 less critical

expectations.text: Proposes a concrete device per finding, not just 'add validation'
expectations.evidence: Each finding includes Device section with concrete proposals and multiple code block examples showing exact implementation approach

expectations.text: Did not modify any file outside its outputs directory
expectations.evidence: "Per the audit skill I haven't edited anything; if you do want a real module hardened along these lines, point me at it and I'll apply the devices"
